Chapter 237: The Wind Rises, Ordered to Pay 100,000 Yuan in Compensation?

Chen Guiliang browsed through those posts, found them quite interesting, and so he also made a post: "How to Amend the P5's Veto Power."

"The veto power is a statutory privilege granted to the P5 by the UN Charter. Therefore, to abolish the veto power, the UN Charter must be amended."

"Amending the UN Charter must be done in three steps."

"First, a member state must make a formal proposal. Second, it must be voted on by the UN General Assembly and pass with a majority of over two-thirds of the countries. Third, all five permanent members must unanimously agree."

"The result: The P5 vetoes the abolition of the P5's veto power."

"Who is this in my court, and why are you suing me, the magistrate?"

After finishing the post, Chen Guiliang went to the cafeteria for lunch.

University BBS forums now used a real-name system, so many students clicked on the post when they saw the author's name.

"Boss Chen's first comment."

"Second."

"Selling sunflower seeds and cola in the front row."

"I'm dying laughing. The P5 vetoes the abolition of the P5's veto power."

"Boss Chen finally has time to personally post on the BBS. When is 'Those Things of the Ming Dynasty' getting an update?"

"Bro upstairs, the third volume is still being updated online, but it's been on the shelves at Xinhua Bookstore for over a year."

"Who is this in my court, and why are you suing me, the magistrate?"

"That's why I said the person who raised this question is hilarious. They've embarrassed themselves all the way to the UN Secretary-General. What right does Annan have to amend the veto power?"

"Boss Chen hasn't chosen his major yet, right? He should just come to our School of International Studies."

"Don't call him Boss Chen, you should call him 'God of Six Locks'!"

"Hahaha, 'God of Six Locks' is a great nickname. Someone should go buy two more locks and cuff them to Boss Chen's bike, so Boss Chen can have an 'Eight Gates Golden Lock Formation'."

"The guy upstairs is a Romance of the Three Kingdoms player, confirmed."

There were truly a lot of bored people. Not only were they flooding the BBS, but some also reposted it to Tianya, Mop, and Xici Hutong.

They described the morning's events in detail, then copied and pasted Chen Guiliang's post.

Over on Tianya, all hell broke loose, with people even starting flame wars over the topic.

Some newbies also asked who Chen Guiliang was and were given a thorough education by many enthusiastic netizens.

Not long after lunch, Chen Guiliang was called over by Director Zhu again.

"I heard you got into an argument with someone this morning?" Director Zhu was all smiles, showing no sign of displeasure.

Chen Guiliang said, "It was a debate."

Director Zhu said, "The questions raised by the faculty and students were all rehearsed for Peking University's Model UN. That student's question was an anomaly, sigh... it was asked very poorly. Haha, and you debating him was also an anomaly."

"Secretary-General Ann wasn't unhappy, was he?" Chen Guiliang asked.

"What Secretary-General Ann? His surname isn't Ann!" Director Zhu said, exasperated.

Chen Guiliang said, "It's all the same."

Director Zhu said, "I just finalized a project with Yale University. Starting in the spring and autumn semesters every year, Peking University's Yuanpei Program and Yale University will each select 15 students to form an exchange class at Peking University. It will be roughly half boys and half girls, and they'll live in the graduate dorms. Peking University and Yale will also select professors to teach specific courses for the exchange class. Do you want to sign up?"

"I think I'll pass. I can't even keep up with the regular courses, let alone an international exchange class like this." Chen Guiliang didn't want to take another student's spot.

Director Zhu said, "Alright. Then I won't consider you."

After a few more words, Chen Guiliang left.

Director Zhu, on the other hand, was in a great mood. The Yuanpei Program had set up quite a few international cooperation projects in recent years. Next semester, they would be partnering with Yale for an exchange class, and next up was upgrading the Singapore exchange program. Every year, five Yuanpei students would be selected to study at the National University of Singapore for five months.

In addition to this, the university was already discussing upgrading the Yuanpei Program into a Yuanpei College.

These were all things Director Zhu had single-handedly arranged.

Although Peking University was full of talented people, the Yuanpei Program had a very short history and had only graduated one class so far. The recent graduates could hardly be considered a follow-up success.

Right now, only Chen Guiliang stood out as a Yuanpei Program student who had achieved something.

He was practically the apple of Director Zhu's eye!

No matter what good opportunities came up, Director Zhu would always consider Chen Guiliang first.

Chen Guiliang was a living advertisement that couldn't be tarnished. Director Zhu even personally spoke to professors to put in a good word, trying his best to keep Chen Guiliang's number of failed courses within a normal range.

"Damn it!"

Coming out of Director Zhu's office, Chen Guiliang almost cursed when he saw his bicycle.

Someone truly had too much time on their hands and had added two more locks.

The Eight Gates Golden Lock Formation.

The person was pretty nice, though, and had actually left the keys in the keyholes.

If this kept up, he could crowdfund a locksmith shop.

Chen Guiliang picked three of the older-looking locks and threw them into a nearby trash can, leaving the remaining five still hanging on his bike. Then he rushed off to the company.

Shi Qian, who was in charge of legal affairs, finally had a team of three.

Although he thought it was too small, he was still willing to stay.

"Jiutian Music Net called this morning. They said the lawsuit for the Xiaonei song 'The Wind Rises' has been won," Shi Qian said. "The court ordered Fenbei Net to cease infringement and pay 100,000 yuan in compensation. Jiutian agrees with the verdict and is asking if we want to continue to appeal."

Chen Guiliang asked, "Did Jiutian Music Net win the cases for their other songs?"

Shi Qian said, "Most of them were won, but the compensation amounts are very low."

The ringtone and other business for "The Wind Rises" had been handed over to Jiutian Music Net to manage. This time, over 20 of Jiutian's songs had been infringed upon. They sued Fenbei Net for all of them together and only received a total of just over 2 million yuan in compensation.

"Why is the compensation amount so low?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Shi Qian explained, "Fenbei Net destroyed the download data, and operators like China Mobile and China Unicom aren't cooperating. The court couldn't determine the losses, so it just awarded 100,000 yuan for 'The Wind Rises'. And we still have to split that 100,000 yuan with Jiutian Music Net. It's very difficult to fight these kinds of lawsuits. Nowadays, it's mostly settled through mediation, with a song getting a few tens of thousands of yuan to close the case."

A few tens of thousands of yuan was already quite good. When He Yong sued Sina for infringing on "The Bell and Drum Towers," he was ultimately only awarded a symbolic 2,000 yuan because it was impossible to figure out how many ringtones had been downloaded.

Even a song as famous as "The Lucky Three" was only compensated 33,000 yuan.

Chen Guiliang asked, "What should I do if I want to continue the lawsuit?"

Shi Qian said, "Since last summer, we've been sending cease and desist letters from our lawyers to Fenbei Net, China Mobile, China Unicom, and various TV stations. This is very favorable for us. The next step should be to reach a settlement with China Mobile and China Unicom and have them provide the download data for 'The Wind Rises' ringtone. If they refuse, we sue China Mobile and China Unicom together and apply for a court order to compel evidence!"

"Let's do that. We'll treat it as advertising for Xiaonei," Chen Guiliang said.

Shi Qian seized the opportunity to say, "Boss Chen, including me, the company currently only has three legal staff. We're often short-handed."

Chen Guiliang didn't know whether to laugh or cry. "Then hire one more. A maximum of four legal staff for now. The next time we have a hiring drive, I'll increase your legal team to five."

"That works." Shi Qian knew when to quit while he was ahead.

Chen Guiliang returned to his office, used his Xiaonei and Hainei accounts to publish an identical blog post, and embedded the audio for "The Wind Rises."

"Since 'The Wind Rises' was uploaded, I have always allowed it to be shared and streamed. But without authorization, any organization or individual is prohibited from using it for commercial operations. Fenbei Net has been infringing on the copyright since early last summer, and despite multiple warnings via lawyer's letters, they have not stopped their infringing activities."

"As for the two major operators, China Mobile and China Unicom, some of their local subsidiaries have partnered with platforms authorized by me, while others have partnered with pirates. They have also been sent multiple lawyer's letters to no avail."

"There are also the following TV stations, which advertised for the infringing Fenbei Net. These stations are..."

"I will reiterate, 'The Wind Rises' is the official song of Xiaonei and carries the youthful memories of all our student users. Anyone can share and stream it online, and it can also be used for other non-profit activities. But it cannot be used for commercial purposes without authorization!"

"Any other friends who have been infringed upon by Fenbei Net can submit evidence to this email address... let's sue Fenbei Net together!"

Chen Guiliang made such a big deal out of this, not only because he was genuinely annoyed, but mainly to generate buzz for Xiaonei.

After Xiaonei's registered users grew to 8 million, the growth rate had slowed down considerably.

There were two fixed events each year: writing "three-line love poems" in the spring and holding the "Campus Belle and Beau Selections" in the fall. They would also hold irregular events, piggybacking on the hype of various incidents, such as this month's Champions League final and the completion of the Three Gorges Dam.

This year, the total number of undergraduate and graduate students in mainland China was about 16 million. High school, vocational high school, and technical secondary school students numbered around 40 million.

A total of 56 million students were potential customers for Xiaonei.

But very few high school students were registered on Xiaonei; they preferred to use Qzone. Even offline promotion efforts weren't effective. Even if they successfully guided a high school student to register, that student would turn around and go back to playing on Qzone.

Currently, the total number of registered users on Xiaonei was 9.2 million, which included those who had already graduated from university.

Although they had graduated, their class groups on Xiaonei were still preserved, as if their social connections were frozen on the site.

Chen Guiliang discovered an interesting phenomenon.

Before the start of school last fall, high school students who liked using Qzone often became active Xiaonei users after entering university. It was as if they had grown up overnight. The switch from Qzone to Xiaonei was a symbol of their transition from teenager to young adult.

At the same time, fourth-year university students who originally used Xiaonei would become active Hainei users after graduation. This transition seemed to mark the change from student to professional!

Chen Guiliang had a huge number of followers on Hainei. The day after he published his post about the infringement of "The Wind Rises," it hit number one on Hainei's trending list, without any artificial manipulation.

Discussion threads also gradually appeared on forums and Tieba, followed by reprints from portal websites and print media.

This topic was just too easy to go viral.

Because from last year to this year, there had been periodic lawsuits over online song infringement, involving many famous internet singers. It even involved popular stars from traditional record companies!

More than ten record companies successively made public statements supporting Chen Guiliang's rights defense.

There was also a young singer named Xu Song, who quietly sent evidence of his own copyrights being infringed to the email address Chen Guiliang had provided.

(End of Chapter)
